subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw own per-agent spend-budget enforcement in the core gateway, or expose only plugin/API primitives for external budget systems?
rationale: The request requires durable budget state, pre-dispatch admission semantics, provider fallback policy, config shape, receipts, and operator recovery UX, which are product-boundary choices rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Core admission layer
options.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets in core with SQLite-backed reservations/refunds, receipts, gateway status/doctor visibility, and tests for fresh install plus upgrade behavior.

options.title: Plugin/API boundary
options.body: Keep core lean by adding or documenting generic admission APIs while a plugin or external policy service owns spend ledgers and operator policy.

options.title: External controls only
options.body: Close native enforcement and document provider accounts, billing proxies, or wallet integrations as the supported budget boundary.

recommendation.title: Core admission layer
recommendation.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets in core with SQLite-backed reservations/refunds, receipts, gateway status/doctor visibility, and tests for fresh install plus upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is primarily product-boundary and operator-safety policy, and this history has adjacent cost-summary and guardrail work.
